title: Delays in Banks’ Loan Loss Provisioning Affect Economic Downturns: Evidence from the U.S. Housing Market

scopes.description: The complete supplied workflow comprises four SAS construction entry points and the Stata analysis entry point. Stage 1 creates delr_call; stage 2 creates foreclosure_my; stage 3 consumes both and creates delr_pre and hmda_13 plus four Stata inputs; stage 4 consumes the stage 1/stage 3 outputs and creates matched_loan.dta; stage 5 loads the four main exports and matched_loan.dta for Tables 2–6. The four packaged .dta files are final-sample identifier lists, not compatible analysis panels, so no analysis_only scope is supported.

issues.description: The archive supplies four SAS construction programs, a Stata analysis program, and four readable identifier lists, but no compatible analysis panels or most required source/prepared tables. Required source routes are recorded individually. Remaining gaps include exact field/history mappings for the author-named coincident, bank-link, reporter, jumbo, CBP, IRS, Census, HPI, and DataQuick/CoreLogic inputs. The intermediate producers and consumers traced in the draft are accounted for; the packaged identifier lists do not establish an analysis_only route.

The supplied SAS LIBNAME/OUTFILE settings and Stata use statements point to absolute Windows paths, and six macro include calls point outside the package even though macro_winsor.sas is supplied beside the scripts. These are staging/path configuration items; the macro itself is present.

The six supplied PROC EXPORT calls spell DBMS=STATA. The SAS/ACCESS 9.4 reference documents DBMS=DTA for Stata .dta import/export, so a coherent six-call DTA alignment is supported working-copy preparation. The coordinator's bounded documentation note also records a historical 9.3 indexed STATA hit but could not retrieve the direct PDF; neither static record establishes the exact installed alias behavior or an execution failure. SAS and SAS/ACCESS runtime availability remain separately unverified in SW_SAS_BASE and SW_SAS_ACCESS_PCFILES.

evidence.description: The appendix documents the 2004–2010 HMDA analysis period and the HMDA-to-Call-Report reporter-panel link.
evidence.quote:
(1) Bank-Level Variables from Call Reports
       I obtain banks’ financial statement data during 2004–2010 from the Call Reports data to
construct the bank-level variables. When I build the bank-level DLR, I extend the sample to 2002
because I require the bank to have at least 12 quarters of financial statements to estimate the
equations (1) and (2).
(2) Mortgage Applications from HMDA
       I obtain mortgage applications during 2004–2010 from the HMDA data. I drop mortgage
applications for amounts less than $1,000 and for which the borrower has income under $10,000
because mortgage values smaller than $1,000 are rounded up to $1,000, and borrower income is
censored at $10,000 (Dell’Ariccia, Igan, and Laeven, 2012). I exclude mortgage applications from
Alaska, Hawaii, and offshore U.S. territories. Additionally, I only use conventional and FHA-
insured mortgages (Loan Type=1 and 2), one to four-family mortgages (Property Type=1), and
home purchase and refinancing mortgages (Loan Purpose=1 and 3). Finally, I eliminate all
application records except the following actions: (i) loan originated, (ii) application approved but
loan not originated, or (iii) application denied. Dell’Ariccia et al. (2012) describe that other actions
represent dubious statuses or loans purchased by other financial institutions, and thus including
them may double-count some of the applications.
        HMDA provides information at the county and the census tract level but not at the ZIP-
code level. To construct the ZIP-code-level data, I match census tracts to ZIP codes using “ZIP
Code Tabulation Area (ZCTA) Relationship Files” from the U.S. census. When a census tract is
not exactly overlapped with one ZIP code, I assign that census tract to a ZIP code containing the
largest population.
(3) Link Call Reports to HMDA

                                                   2

        Linking Call Reports to HMDA is a critical task in the analysis. HMDA provides a
“Reporter Panel,” which contains information about all institutions that are reported under HMDA.
I identify the same lenders by matching RSSD9001 in Call Reports and Respondent RSSD ID in
Reporter Panel. Then, I merge the reporter panel with mortgage applications based on the same
Respondent ID and the same Agency Code.

evidence.description: The appendix distinguishes the DataQuick assessor, transaction, and loan files and describes their separate contents.
evidence.quote:
(3) DataQuick
        DataQuick is proprietary data containing information on real estate appraisal and
transactions in the U.S. and was made available through the Fama-Miller Center for Research in
Finance and the Initiative on Global Markets at the University of Chicago Booth School of
Business. 1 DataQuick consists of three main files: assessor, transaction, and loan. The assessor file
contains information on individual properties used to assess property taxes, such as appraised
values. The transaction file includes information about theproperty’s sale, such as an indicator for
distressed sales and buyers and sellers’ information. Finally, the loan file contains information
about the financing of home purchases, such as the value of loans taken and interest rates.
